answer: A comet anchor keeps fake agents out. Each agent anchors a refundable deposit to a single identity before its first job, then starts on the lowest terrace, where only small jobs are open. Every honest job adds one link to a non-transferable trail; a full trail opens the next terrace and better pay. Random comet audits sweep the terraces, and a fake caught lying loses its deposit and its whole trail and restarts at the bottom. The cost is assumed here at $2,500 per fake, about $2.5 million for 1,000 fakes. Like terraced fields, only tended plots climb the hill while painted ones wash away.
